audit.whatIsWrong: Content layer paints Aurora winning levels 3 through 2+ items while Malzahar holds a 54.98% win rate over 1617 games; full layer already reads Skill from level 3 on.
audit.why: Malzahar's shove-and-suppress pattern neutralises her after Q max; the two layers also contradict each other row by row.
audit.corrected: Early is Aurora's (900-range Q recast poke), level 3 onward is a skill matchup around Across the Veil and Nether Grasp timers.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and spikes[2] treat every spike as Aurora's; spikes name a fabricated 'W (Explosive Spirit)' and a 'true-damage passive' that is actually a heal.
audit.why: Her W is Across the Veil, her passive Spirit Abjuration heals off exorcised spirits — no true damage in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: Malzahar spikes at Lost Chapter (shove engine), 6 (point-and-click suppress) and Liandry's; Aurora spikes at Q max and roam timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood/tldr reference poking 'his shield off' — Aurora has no shield; the shield in this lane is Malzahar's own passive. No mention that Between Worlds' CC can break Nether Grasp, or that her healing passive rewards anti-heal.
audit.why: Template written for a shielded male enemy; missing-interactions file flags both omissions.
audit.corrected: Trade window is Across the Veil down (22s rank 1); Q (6s) silences her Q recast; suppress only after Between Worlds is spent; her P heals through chip.

audit.whatIsWrong: 18 misgendered fields (Aurora called he/him), two copy-paste-bleed bullets, cooldowns field with no digit, one unsupported magnitude.

edits.before: Level 1 is even as both champs just farm with light poke.
edits.after: Level 1 is hers: her 900-range Q pokes while you just farm.

edits.before: Level 2 stays even before her hop mobility fully out-trades you.
edits.after: Level 2 stays hers: Q-recast poke chips you before your W is up.

edits.before: Level 3 favors Aurora once Q poke plus W hops out-trade and dodge your kit.
edits.after: Level 3 evens out: E-W shove and Q silence answer her step-ups and hops.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 favor Aurora because her mobility harasses you and dodges your Q.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even: Lost Chapter shove taxes her, but her W dodges your Q.

edits.before: Level 6 favors Aurora as her W and R let her bait and side-step your suppress.
edits.after: Level 6 is even: her W can bait your suppress, but Grasp plus a gank kills her.

edits.before: First item favors Aurora since her mobility and true damage out-trade and out-roam you.
edits.after: First item is even: Liandry's makes your shove lethal, though her hops still dodge Q.

edits.before: 2+ items favor Aurora because her resets let her fight when your Nether Grasp is down.
edits.after: 2+ items is a skill check: she strikes when Nether Grasp is down, you suppress her carry.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a skill matchup: you both farm and poke, but Aurora's bounce Q already threatens to chip you if you step up carelessly.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are Aurora's: her 900-range Q and recast chip you for free, so farm with E and keep the passive shield up as you step up.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 belong to Aurora because her Q poke plus W spirit-hops let her out-trade you and dodge your Q, and her mobility means even your Nether Grasp can be baited and side-stepped.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 even out: your E-W shove taxes her tower and your Q silence stops her Q recast, while her 22s Across the Veil is the one tool that dodges Nether Grasp — track it before committing.

edits.before: Aurora keeps the edge into items: her hop resets and R banish let her choose the fight while your suppress is down, so respect her all-in, itemize a cleanse, and lean on your team to lock her.
edits.after: Into items it is a skill check: she picks fights when your 140s Nether Grasp is down, while one suppression on her flank erases her — hold R for her commit and let the Liandry's burn do the rest.

edits.before: Aurora's spike: her Q (Twofold Hex) bounce poke and W (Explosive Spirit) hop let her harass you and dodge your Q line, chunking you every time you walk up to shove the wave.
edits.after: Aurora's spike: her Q (Twofold Hex) recast poke and W (Across the Veil) hop let her harass you and dodge your Q line, chunking you every time you walk up to shove the wave.

edits.before: Even her ult beats you here: her R (Between Worlds) plus W dashes let her disengage the moment you threaten Nether Grasp, so she can bait your suppress and reposition out of it.
edits.after: Your 6 matters too: Nether Grasp is point-and-click, so she must hold W (22s) or R (Between Worlds) to escape it — if either is down, your suppress into E burn is a guaranteed chunk.

edits.before: Aurora stays ahead: her E (The Weirding) spirit-hop mobility and true-damage passive out-trade your point-blank kit, and she can roam off your shoved wave faster than you punish.
edits.after: First item is a race: Liandry's makes your shove and suppress lethal, while her E (The Weirding) slow-and-hop plus W stealth let her disengage and roam if you leave rivers unwarded.

edits.before: Aurora out-scales this lane: her repeated W hops and R banish let her pick when to fight your suppress down, so you must build a cleanse and play tightly with your team to answer her.
edits.after: Late is a stand-off: her W and R let her pick fights while Nether Grasp (80s at rank 3) is down, but one suppression erases her — shield up, hold a flank, and press R on her commit.

edits.after: Aurora wins by chipping you with Twofold Hex recasts, dodging your combo with Across the Veil, and roaming off your waves.

edits.after: Poke-and-punish: land E when she steps up to farm, then Q-silence her Q recast — with Across the Veil down (22s) she cannot dodge the full rotation.

edits.after: Trading into her with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.

edits.after: Q online: the silence is your trade answer. Use it on her Q recast or W hop, not poke she walks around.

edits.after: W voidlings turn your shove permanent — the wave hits her tower while you ward, roam-shadow, or just exist safely.

edits.before: Post-6 every lane state includes the Grasp threat: shove, ward, and punish anyone who walks into point-and-click range. With a jungler nearby, your R is a written guarantee.
edits.after: Post-6 every lane state includes the Grasp threat — but Between Worlds' CC can break your channel, so suppress after her R is spent. With a jungler nearby, your R is a guarantee.
